messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1: elevated 5xx rate from our inference frontends in aws-us-west-2 (predominantly azc and azd). Alert: ELB returns 502/503 from upstreams. service=redwood-api, scope=production. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/2314506789

alex: seeing spikes on the global proxy and high connection queue on ELB. 503s started ~3m ago. health checks toggling between healthy/unhealthy for a subset of targets.

leah: paging oncall. @nick you up? can you confirm if this is an AZ-level connectivity issue or backend saturation?

nick: oncall here. I have console open. ELB targetgroup shows ~40% of targets in azc failing 502, azd looks degraded but not as bad. CPU on some inference hosts is normal. noticing lots of TCP resets to ENIs in azc.

emily: customer reports: increased latency and intermittent failures for batch embedding jobs in us-west-2. multiple customers hitting retries. tracking ticket #C-6729.

rohan: running quick checks on Route53 health checks — no global DNS change. DNS latencies are fine. This looks like intra-region network flakiness between AZs.

leah: can we try routing a small percentage of traffic away from azc to azb/candidate region? prefer weight change instead of full failover.

nick: agree. preparing weighted routing change on our traffic manager. will start with 10% -> azb and monitor.

infra-bot: deploy status: no recent infra deployments in last 30m. No config rollouts match service=redwood-api.

alex: quick note: KV cache hitrate for conversational cache dropped in azc. Likely due to connection issues to cache nodes (internal memcached cluster in azc). Could amplify backend load.

nick: executing routing weight tweak now:
```bash
# adjust route weights via traffic-manager
traffic-manager update --region us-west-2 --from azc=60,azd=30,azb=10
```

nick: done. starting to see small drop in 5xxs for requests routed to azb, overall error rate down 8% so far. continuing monitoring.

leah: start preparing for target replacement in azc. may need to drain and reprovision a subset to clear conntrack/ENI state. prioritize KV-cache nodes and inference hosts with high reset counts.

emily: notifying affected customers with initial impact statement: "We are investigating intermittent 5xx errors for inference in us-west-2. We have shifted a portion of traffic and are mitigating. We will post updates every 15 minutes."

rohan: checking AWS console: some EC2 instances in azc show ENI attach/detach events and connection issues to the AZ NAT gateway. Filing a support case with AWS (case 0456789012) — asking for networking fabric check.

alex: running targeted drain on 6 unhealthy targets in azc (manual deregister with timeout 10s) to force traffic away while we reprovision.

nick: command I ran:
```bash
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456:targetgroup/tg-redwood-api/abcdef --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h
```

alex: after deregister, connection queues on ELB decreased, but some long-lived connections still show resets. Could be NAT conntrack exhaustion.

leah: scaling natgw in azc + add extra EIPs to spread connections. Also increasing conntrack timeout on our customer-facing proxy nodes as a stopgap.

rohan: AWS replied to support case: "Investigating increased control-plane events in us-west-2azc causing intermittent packet drops in ENIs. No immediate global cause found." Requesting ASG replacement for problematic hosts.

emily: update to customers: "We have shifted more traffic off the affected AZ and reduced error rates by ~70% compared to peak. Some customers may still see intermittent failures while we remediate."

nick: performing rolling replace on a subset of cache+inference nodes in azc. will do 2 at a time. expected 12-18m.

alex: monitoring graphs: 5xx count back near baseline for most endpoints, minor blips for long-tail requests. embedding job retry rate down 60%.

leah: important: keep Route53 TTLs unchanged to avoid DNS churn. Any further routing should be via traffic-manager weight/ELB target management.

rohan: AWS follow-up: "We've applied a fabric-level mitigation to reduce packet loss in azc. Monitoring. Recommend ASG replace and avoid heavy connection churn for 30m."

nick: completed rolling replaces in azc (6 hosts replaced). Post-replace healthchecks back to healthy.

emily: customer comms: posting "full mitigation steps applied; traffic moved gradually and faulty hosts replaced; AWS is monitoring the AZ fabric; additional follow-ups will be sent when we confirm long-term stability."

leah: handoff note for night oncall: if error rate creeps above 5% of baseline, escalate to infra and re-run traffic-manager shift to 20% azb. Documented runbook steps: https://wiki.redwood.internal/incidents/runbooks/az-network-flap

nick: adding short timeline for postmortem: root suspected: transient AZ network fabric issues causing ENI packet drops and conntrack exhaustion, amplified by KV cache misses triggering backend surge. Immediate mitigation: traffic-weight shift, targeted host replacement, NATGW scaling, AWS support engagement.

alex: thumbs: :thumbsup: Good work team. Will start PM to open postmortem and gather logs (pcap if AWS will provide).

incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED (mitigated) at ts=2314507012. Postmortem owner assigned: leah.

leah: will draft postmortem and share timeline + impact numbers. Early estimate: ~12 minutes of high-error window affecting ~3% of requests in us-west-2, several customer retries/failures (C-6729 and C-6731).

emily: closing customer updates now and scheduling follow-up with affected accounts. Thanks everyone."
